summary: Aermotor tower moved to Jacksonville's Forestry Tower Park in 1938; fire lookout until 1992; standing and not open to the public.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor steel tower (register); Weebly describes a 100-foot steel tower

access.note: Register says the tower is not open to the public. The surrounding grounds are a city park.

events.note: Moved to the present site (register, park history). Weebly says erected by the CCC; the Florida chapter report says re-erected there.
Renamed Southside Fire Tower (park history; blog says late 1950s). The register gives 1938 for the rename.
Last year the tower was used as a fire detection facility
Division of Forestry closed the operation
Designated a local landmark after residents and neighborhood associations pushed for protection
City bought the tract for a park
Registered March 16, 2015; nominated by Bob Spear

corrections.why: The register says the tower is not open to the public.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says renamed Southside in 1938; park history says 1959; blog says late 1950s. Recorded the rename as 1959, following the park history and blog, and kept the register's 1938 date in the event note.
Register and park history agree the tower was moved in 1938; Weebly says erected then; the Florida chapter says re-erected. Recorded as relocation, not new construction.

sources.title: Fire Tower, Beach Boulevard, Windy Hill

notes_for_editor: Original build date is not in any source (register gives no year for the State's build). Brief's access 'unknown' corrected to closed. The Weebly Flagler page (Wadsworth record) attaches a 1959 Southside rename to a Flagler County tower; that conflicts with the park history. The Florida chapter report asks whether the Jacksonville Heights tower was re-erected as Southside; unverified, not used. No new photos added.
